Indian Standard
GUIDELINES FOR UTILIZATION AND DISPOSAL OF SOLID WASTES FROM INTEGRATED STEEL PLANTS
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 28 February 1983, after the draft finalized by the Solid Wastes Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 In any industry when basic raw materials are processed, along with the main products some other materials are also produced. Depending on the characteristics of these materials some of them, called by-products, may be economically used either in the same industry or in another industry, whereas the rest, called wastes, are totally discarded. 0.2.1 An Indian integrated iron and steel plant produces approximately This I.1 tonne of solid wastes for every tonne of ingot steel produced. figure does not include ore fines and slimes of ore crushing plant at mines, and middlings or rejects at a coal washery. 0.3 Dumping sites of the solid wastes preferred for recycle should be For example, solid wastes located adjacent to the recycle process units. which are to be recycled to sintering plant should be dumped in close proximity to the sintering plant for effective recycling.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes guidelines for the present and possible future uses of the solid wastes generated in an integrated steel plant. Amount of generation and characteristics of these wastes have also been given. 1.2 This standard does not cover wastes generated at mines and collieries. It also does not include spillage at various stages of processing which is recycled into the system, for example, dust at coke ovens, sinter plant, etc, and also wastes generated in small quantities like dust from open hearth furnaces and sludge from water softening plants. 3

2.6 FlueDust - The gas emitted by a blast furnace is laden with dust as it comes out of the furnace. During the gas cleaning process, the coarser particles, collected in the dust catcher, are called flue dust. 2.7 Fly AshFly ash is a finely divided combustion of ground of powdered coal and gases of boilers fired by pulverized coal. 2.8 Foundry Wastes a) Foundry Sand - Large amount of used silica sand, is burnt, generated as a waste in the foundry. b) Cupola and Electric Furnace Slag - A slag generated or electrical furnace melting. a part of which during cupola residue carried resulting from the along with the flue

2.9 Mill&aleWhile steel ingots or other sections are heated in soaking pits or reheating furnaces before rolling, the outer skin of the material is oxidised. The oxidised layer, called mill scale, drops down in the furnaces or under the rolling table. 2.10 Slimes - During crushing and washing of iron ore within the steel plant for improving its quality and size, finer Yfraction ( less than 200 urn ) These fine is carried away by water in the form of slurry `into a pond. particles of iron ore are called slimes. 2.11 LD Converter/Open Hearth Slag -This material is generated during conversion of iron into steel in a steel making furnace.
